headline: High-risk default write-and-network orchestration can cascade into unsafe actions; prompt-injection and leakage are lower but nonzero.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: CrewAI has shared-memory, tool-using multi-agent orchestration and broad I/O surfaces; mem0 is a memory layer that can feed prior content back into prompts. That creates a plausible instruction-hijack path if untrusted content is stored and later re-read. The pair lacks documented provenance controls, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF mem0 stores attacker-controlled text that CrewAI later reuses as prompt context
IF CrewAI agents read shared memory without provenance filtering
mitigations: Tag memory entries with source and trust level
Strip instructions from retrieved memory before prompting
Disable automatic reuse of untrusted memories
Add a human review step for externally sourced content
requires-engineering: implement provenance-aware prompt assembly

B_data_leakage.rationale: CrewAI can read/write the host working directory and handle API keys, while mem0 is a knowledge-management component with no declared network egress. The pair can leak data if sensitive crew inputs are persisted into shared memory or files, but mem0’s lack of egress and absent shared workspace details keep blast radius limited and configuration-dependent.
conditions: IF CrewAI writes sensitive crew inputs into files or memory that mem0 later indexes
IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace or memory store
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent
Store secrets outside shared memory
Redact sensitive fields before indexing
Rotate any exposed API keys
requires-engineering: add access controls on the memory store

C_capability_conflict.rationale: CrewAI can write the filesystem and spawn subprocesses, but mem0 exposes no write or network capabilities in the profile. Without overlapping mutable-resource writes, direct capability conflict is limited. The main uncertainty is that mem0’s missing I/O details could hide writes, so the safer choice is low rather than none.
conditions: IF mem0 is configured with a writable shared store or filesystem not shown in the profile
IF both agents target the same mutable directory
mitigations: Assign distinct output directories
Run only one writer at a time
Disable unnecessary subprocess tools
Use file locks for shared artifacts
requires-engineering: add explicit concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: CrewAI’s role-playing agents can generate outputs that mem0 may preserve and later surface as memory, creating a default path where one agent’s content becomes another’s authoritative context. Because CrewAI can also act through tools and subprocesses, a mistaken memory entry can cascade into downstream actions. The pair lacks built-in verification guarantees, so high is warranted.
conditions: IF mem0 returns CrewAI-generated memories to later prompts without verification
IF CrewAI agents act on retrieved memories as facts or instructions
mitigations: Require citation or source checks before acting
Mark memory as advisory, not authoritative
Add a verification prompt before tool use
Limit tool permissions for action-taking agents
requires-engineering: build a validation gate between memory and action

E_compliance.rationale: CrewAI explicitly handles API keys and developer-passed crew data, while mem0 is a memory system with no declared residency or retention controls in the profile. This creates a compliance mismatch risk if regulated data is stored in mem0 or routed through CrewAI logs, but the profile does not show a specific regulated-data class or mandatory cross-border flow, so low is appropriate.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in mem0 without matching retention/deletion controls
IF CrewAI logs or forwards secrets into a different jurisdiction or retention regime
mitigations: Avoid storing regulated data in shared memory
Set short retention on logs and memories
Document deletion/export procedures
Mask secrets before logging
requires-engineering: align retention and residency policies
